currentContext.expansion: Sagility is an asset-light services business, so expansion is expressed as delivery footprint, capability build-out and acquisitions rather than plant capex. The Company delivers services through its tools and platforms and its talent pool from 31 global service delivery locations across India, the Philippines, the U.S., Jamaica and Colombia; the Board's Report notes this multi-geography footprint combines onshore and nearshore locations in the U.S., Jamaica and Colombia with offshore centres in India and the Philippines, a diversified base that reduces dependence on any single country and supports business continuity. Delivery capacity is scaled through people - a workforce of more than 46,000 professionals worldwide, including clinicians and technology specialists - supported by dynamic workforce management, cross-trained talent pools and multi-geo scalable delivery infrastructure that allows capacity to be aligned to fluctuating client volumes. Footprint expansion is also pursued through M&A: the BroadPath Healthcare Solutions acquisition is described as a strategic step towards entering the mid- and small-market segment, broadening the client base and service portfolio, with its integration and contribution extending Sagility's market reach and complementing its service portfolio. Capability expansion is directed at adjacent, higher-value areas - clinical services and pharmacy benefit management, patient support offerings for PBMs and specialty pharmacy players, and scaling end-to-end Revenue Cycle Management within the provider segment - alongside continued investment in AI, platform-led capabilities and integrated operating models that connect fragmented workflows, plus proprietary platform integration inside client workflows to raise switching costs. Cost-side footprint actions include proactive geo-shifts and a multi-shore delivery model to optimise cost structures. Management states that improvements in margins, operational rigor and balance sheet strength have enhanced the Company's capacity to invest with purpose, with investments directed toward initiatives that reinforce competitive advantage. No named plant, site-commissioning or dated capacity-addition project is disclosed in the provided sections.

risks.risk: Total dependence on a single end-market: the entire revenue base comes from the U.S. healthcare industry, with exports contributing 100% of turnover
risks.note: Exposes Sagility to U.S. regulatory, economic and outsourcing-related developments - healthcare policy shifts, proposed measures such as the HIRE Act and state-level anti-outsourcing bills. Mitigations cited: deepening presence across both payer and provider segments, expanding into adjacent higher-value areas such as clinical services and pharmacy benefit management, regulatory-compliance and information-security focus, a multi-country delivery footprint (U.S., Jamaica, Colombia onshore/nearshore; India and the Philippines offshore) and negligible dependency on H1B visas.

risks.risk: Client concentration and client restructuring - the top 10 client groups contribute 83.9% of total revenue
risks.note: Consolidation, mergers, acquisitions or restructuring among healthcare payers and providers may cause vendor rationalization, contract renegotiation, volume reallocation or pricing pressure. Mitigations: diversifying across payer and provider segments, scaling end-to-end RCM in providers, higher-value clinical/patient-support offerings for PBMs and specialty pharmacy, multi-year performance-linked contracts, the BroadPath-led entry into mid- and small-market accounts, and proactive engagement during client M&A.

risks.risk: Fluctuation in client business volumes, including the risk of clients insourcing work
risks.note: Revenues are linked to client-driven transaction volumes that can swing with membership trends, cost pressures, regulatory change, outsourcing decisions or client reprioritisation, affecting revenue predictability, capacity utilization and operating leverage. Mitigated through diversified revenue streams, flexible operating models, multi-year and outcome-based constructs, dynamic workforce management, cross-trained talent and multi-geo scalable delivery, plus platform integration that raises client dependence and reduces insourcing likelihood.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity and pricing pressure from global outsourcing providers, broad-based IT/business services firms, specialised healthcare-focused companies and clients' own in-house/digital capabilities
risks.note: Competition combined with client cost-efficiency focus drives evolving commercial constructs and pricing dynamics. Sagility responds with an integrated domain-led operating model, a shift to outcome-based and managed-services constructs (value-led rather than price-led), non-linear output-based commercial models, expansion into higher-value clinical and adjacent lines, geo-shifts/multi-shore cost optimisation, and regular monitoring of account margins with periodic reporting to leadership.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity and data privacy - handling sensitive protected health information across a partly remote workforce
risks.note: Data breaches or non-compliance with stringent U.S. and global data-protection regimes (HIPAA, HITECH, CCPA, GDPR) could trigger regulatory action, financial penalties, lost business and reputational damage; delayed incident reporting is itself a compliance exposure. Controls include encryption, identity management, access controls and network protection, periodic risk assessments, vulnerability testing and independent external reviews, privacy impact assessments, data mapping, third-party data-sharing controls, a defined incident-management process owned by Compliance and Cybersecurity, training and awareness, and market-benchmarked cyber insurance.

risks.risk: Talent management, attrition and wage inflation in a competitive talent market, including key-management succession
risks.note: Elevated attrition and wage inflation affect service continuity, cost structures and margin profile; permanent-employee voluntary attrition (above 90 days) was 29.4% in FY 2026 versus 27.5% in FY 2025. Loss of senior leaders who hold deep domain expertise and long-standing client relationships could impair client confidence and service continuity. Mitigated through competitive, market-aligned compensation and benefits programmes.

risks.risk: Regulatory compliance complexity from operating across multiple geographies
risks.note: Frequent regulatory change increases compliance complexity and multi-jurisdiction operations increase legal exposure; non-compliance may result in penalties, financial strain and reputational damage. Managed through periodic Legal-team oversight, regular compliance status reporting (including exceptions) to Senior Management, the Audit Committee and the Board, and refreshing compliance frameworks as regulations evolve.

Unethical practices may invite regulatory scrutiny and penalties, and misconduct can damage brand reputation and stakeholder trust, potentially reducing investor confidence and access to financing. Addressed through a formal whistleblower mechanism allowing confidential reporting, with matters reviewed under established protocols and the code of conduct.

one-line thesis: A clean beat on every line — revenue **+27.6% (+15.2% CC)**, adjusted EBITDA **+27.9%**, adjusted PAT **+35.1%**, adjusted **ROCE >50%**, net debt down to **0.06x** — delivered while absorbing annual increments *and* a genuinely large statutory shock: **Karnataka and Telangana minimum-wage revisions**, worth **~120bps of FY27 adjusted EBITDA**, hitting a base where **65–70% of headcount sits in Bangalore and Hyderabad**. Management held the **24–25% margin guidance** anyway, explicitly funded by **FX (+100bps in Q1)** plus efficiency initiatives — an honest admission that the offset is partly not operational. The strategic direction is the more interesting story: a shift from *"fragmented process-led models"* to **managed-service deals where Sagility owns the workflow end-to-end and commits to a cost takeout** — underpinned by commissioned Everest Group research showing **70% of payers claim AI adoption but only 10% report measurable improvement**, which is precisely the wedge for an integrator. The most conservative thing on the call: after 14.9% CC organic growth in Q1, guidance stayed at **low double digits**, and the CEO refused three separate invitations to raise it.

segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Payer operations (89.6% of revenue):** the core. Growth led by **expansion within existing relationships**, with **FY26-added clients beginning to scale**. No pricing lever was used — see §7.
- **Providers (10.4%):** RCM. Management has looked at RCM acquisition targets and passed: *"a lot of the RCM targets that came out didn't clearly add to our capabilities and the valuations were pretty high."*
- **CareSeed (closed 11-Jun-2026):** Kansas City, founded 2012, **14-person team**, **CY25 revenue $5.1mn at 31.4% EBITDA margin with 95% recurring revenue**, **30 small/mid payer clients (26 new to Sagility)**. Two platforms: **Forecast** (HEDIS reporting & quality analytics) and **Harvest** (cloud-based medical-record review and chart abstraction). The acquisition thesis has four pillars — capability (quality for **Medicare Advantage**: HEDIS, CMS Stars, care-gap orchestration), technology, cross-sell into 26 mid-market clients, and talent with established client relationships.
- **The CareSeed value-chain extension is the important part:** Sagility can attach **chart abstraction** to the platform, **create the chase list**, integrate Forecast/Harvest with its own **population-health AIP platform** (care coach/care manager workflow), and then go beyond identifying care gaps to **closing** them via member outreach and behavioural change — *"health plans can move beyond HEDIS reporting to member level orchestration, while unlocking star improvement and revenue uplift."*
- **BroadPath:** ~**$13.5–13.6mn** in Q1, now fully merged — *"it's very difficult to say, is it a BroadPath client or a Sagility client, right? It's a combined team now."* It is the main reason seasonal revenue doubled from ~3% to ~6% of the total (Medicare sales and enrolment support).
- **Sagility Synchrony:** AI-led orchestration platform connecting fragmented claims and adjustment workflows — *"making inroads"*, no revenue disclosed.
- **A top-5 client cohort is going backwards for a good reason:** a large line of business is being **migrated from onshore to offshore delivery**, which reduces revenue but management confirms is **margin-accretive**.

- **Mid- and small-market expansion** — **55+ mid-market clients** added across BroadPath and CareSeed; cross-sell described as *"pretty high"* opportunity in mid-market, but the CareSeed **platform** is unlikely to sell into large payers (who already have quality-reporting vendors) — only the **combined platform + services package** could.
- **Quality / Medicare Advantage Stars** — new capability, structurally growing as payers chase Stars-linked revenue.

capital allocation: Deliberate deleveraging alongside bolt-on M&A: **net debt ₹1,110mn (0.06x)** with a commitment to **fully repay outstanding debt during FY27**, cutting finance cost further (already a driver of PAT more than doubling since FY24). **₹9,674mn cash** on hand described as flexibility for strategic initiatives. **Adjusted ROCE >50%**, **cash conversion ~70%**. M&A is capability-led, disciplined on valuation (**RCM targets passed on price**), and structured so that CareSeed's 31.4% EBITDA margin business is **accretive to margin**, not dilutive. A **~3% ESOP pool** is approved-in-process but ungranted — a future, unquantified P&L charge.
risks & watch-items:
1. **Q2 absorbs the full minimum-wage impact — "more than double" Q1's 40bps** — against a 24–25% guide that is already partly FX-funded.
2. **The margin defence relies on currency.** If the rupee reverses, the 120bps has nothing to lean on but efficiency, which takes **12–18 months**.
3. **Hedges taken at lower rates** mean **reported** EBITDA/EPS will not enjoy the FX benefit that flatters adjusted EBITDA.
4. **No pricing power at all** — stated outright. Growth must come entirely from volume, scope and new logos while clients push prices *down*.
5. **AI deflation is guided to rise from 100–150bps to ~200bps and "maybe even go higher"** — a permanent, self-inflicted revenue headwind inherent to the model.
6. **Client concentration is increasing**, not decreasing — *"if you can see the percentage of our top three, top five, they also continue to increase"* — even as 55+ mid-market clients were bought in.
7. **A top-5 cohort is shrinking** on an onshore→offshore migration. Margin-positive, revenue-negative, and it will recur.
8. **Managed-service deals take 3–6 months of conversation**; the shift to outcome-based revenue is real but slow, and effort-based pricing still dominates.
9. **Only 1 new logo** in Q1's $35.3mn ACV — growth is overwhelmingly farming, not hunting.
10. **Adjusted vs reported gap is wide** (earnouts, SARs, intangible amortisation, the ₹151mn exceptional, the one-time wage item). Every headline metric on this call is an adjusted one.
11. **Open-enrolment volumes unknowable until September** — the single biggest determinant of H2, and management said so.
12. **Peers are reportedly seeing payer spending tighten**; Sagility says it is not, *"at least we are not seeing in the conversations that we are having."* Watch for divergence.
13. **The ~3% ESOP pool** is an unquantified future dilution/charge.
14. **CareSeed's platform may not scale to large payers** — management conceded most large clients already have quality-reporting vendors; only a packaged platform+services play could enter.
management quality / tone: Unusually disciplined disclosure. They gave a **quantified margin bridge in basis points**, split the minimum-wage hit into its in-quarter (₹70mn) and exceptional (₹151mn) components, disclosed the **exact geographic exposure (65–70% of headcount)** that makes the shock large, admitted the FX crutch when asked directly (*"Both, right? Currency has played a part"*), and volunteered the adjusted-vs-reported hedge distinction unprompted. They **refused to raise guidance three times** off a 14.9% CC organic quarter, and refused to extrapolate 5.1% sequential growth (*"I wouldn't read too much into it"*). Two answers were "we'll come back to you" (the FY26-cohort growth split; BroadPath revenue), which for a company that has now made two acquisitions is a fair ask to follow up. The one moment of edge — *"Baidik, you're asking the same question multiple ways"* — read as conviction rather than irritation. Overall this is management being **structurally conservative into a strong quarter**, which is the right posture ahead of a full-quarter wage hit.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The Everest data point — 70% of payers have "adopted AI", only 10% see measurable improvement — is the single most valuable disclosure on the call.** It reframes AI from a threat to a BPM's addressable problem: piecemeal AI fails, end-to-end workflow redesign is required, and only a domain-deep operator can do that redesign.
- **Insourcing is economically impossible for cost-pressured payers** because the work sits offshore. Cost pressure on clients is therefore a *tailwind*, not a risk — the exact inverse of the usual outsourcing-cycle worry.
- **Sagility has zero pricing power and is growing 15% CC anyway.** All of it is volume/scope. That is a stronger signal about demand than any pricing-led beat would be.
- **The margin guide is being defended with FX, and management said so.** The underlying operating margin is *not* comfortably absorbing 120bps yet — mitigation is 12–18 months out.
- **Deliberate geographic de-risking has begun** — Indore, Tamil Nadu, Mumbai — driven not by cost arbitrage but by **regulatory wage risk concentration** in Karnataka/Telangana. Expect this to become a structural cost line.
- **CareSeed is tiny ($5.1mn) but bought at 31.4% EBITDA margin with 95% recurring revenue and 26 new logos** — the client list and the Medicare-Advantage quality capability are the assets; the revenue is rounding.
- **Seasonality doubled (3% → 6% of revenue) because of BroadPath**, and is now a permanent feature of the Q1 and Q2 optics. Sequential declines in Q1 are structural, not signals.
- **Attrition improving from 38.1% to 28.6% in one quarter** is a large, under-discussed cost and quality tailwind in a 47,307-person business.
- **Present in only 7 of the top 10 national insurers, and entry to the rest must come through clinical and payment integrity** — the traditional claims/enrolment work at those accounts is already placed elsewhere. That is a precise, checkable roadmap.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Sagility is a U.S.-healthcare-focused, tech-enabled business process management firm positioning itself as the "Decision Intelligence and Outcomes layer" for healthcare operations across payers, providers and pharmacy benefit managers.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Sagility manages and improves mission-critical administrative, financial and clinical workflows exclusively for the U.S. healthcare industry, serving payers, providers and pharmacy benefit managers with over 26 years of domain experience. Its end-to-end capabilities span member and provider lifecycle management, claims operations, clinical utilization and care management, payment integrity and provider revenue cycle management, delivered through a global footprint across the United States, India, the Philippines, Jamaica and Colombia with a workforce of over 46,000 professionals including clinicians and technology specialists. The company serves more than 80 healthcare client enterprises, including several of the largest health plans and pharmacy benefit managers in the United States, and has evolved its operating model from AI-enabled to AI-embedded operations.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Payer operations (89.6% of revenue):** the core. Growth led by **expansion within existing relationships**, with **FY26-added clients beginning to scale**. No pricing lever was used — see §7.
- **Providers (10.4%):** RCM. Management has looked at RCM acquisition targets and passed: *"a lot of the RCM targets that came out didn't clearly add to our capabilities and the valuations were pretty high."*
- **CareSeed (closed 11-Jun-2026):** Kansas City, founded 2012, **14-person team**, **CY25 revenue $5.1mn at 31.4% EBITDA margin with 95% recurring revenue**, **30 small/mid payer clients (26 new to Sagility)**. Two platforms: **Forecast** (HEDIS reporting & quality analytics) and **Harvest** (cloud-based medical-record review and chart abstraction). The acquisition thesis has four pillars — capability (quality for **Medicare Advantage**: HEDIS, CMS Stars, care-gap orchestration), technology, cross-sell into 26 mid-market clients, and talent with established client relationships.
- **The CareSeed value-chain extension is the important part:** Sagility can attach **chart abstraction** to the platform, **create the chase list**, integrate Forecast/Harvest with its own **population-health AIP platform** (care coach/care manager workflow), and then go beyond identifying care gaps to **closing** them via member outreach and behavioural change — *"health plans can move beyond HEDIS reporting to member level orchestration, while unlocking star improvement and revenue uplift."*
- **BroadPath:** ~**$13.5–13.6mn** in Q1, now fully merged — *"it's very difficult to say, is it a BroadPath client or a Sagility client, right? It's a combined team now."* It is the main reason seasonal revenue doubled from ~3% to ~6% of the total (Medicare sales and enrolment support).
- **Sagility Synchrony:** AI-led orchestration platform connecting fragmented claims and adjustment workflows — *"making inroads"*, no revenue disclosed.
- **A top-5 client cohort is going backwards for a good reason:** a large line of business is being **migrated from onshore to offshore delivery**, which reduces revenue but management confirms is **margin-accretive**.

order_book.body: **$35.3mn of steady-state ACV signed in Q1**, spread across **18 existing clients and 1 new logo** — consistent with a pattern management flagged of **15–20 clients per quarter for at least the last three or four quarters**, i.e. growth is broad-based rather than concentrated in one large win. Managed-service/outcome-based deals are in **active conversation for three to six months** each and remain the timing risk (*"deal timing can be difficult to predict"*). Cross-sell pipeline: **six or seven active opportunities in BroadPath clients**; CareSeed cross-sell just beginning. Penetration into the **top 10 US national insurers is 7 of 10** — the remaining three are long-time outsourcers whose traditional work is already placed, so entry must come via **clinical** and **payment integrity**, areas they have not outsourced to the same extent.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **FY27 revenue: low double-digit ORGANIC growth in constant currency — REITERATED**, despite Q1 delivering **14.9% CC organic**. Pressed three separate ways by two analysts, the CEO would not raise it: *"we are still guiding to low double-digit growth... Will it be exactly that number, plus, minus some number? But yes, definitely, we are reasonably confident of delivering the double-digit number."*
- **FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin: 24–25% MAINTAINED**, explicitly *"despite absorbing 120 basis points incremental impact from minimum wage increases in Karnataka and Telangana."* Upside flagged: *"If the eventual outcome on minimum wages results in a lower impact, we could be at the upper end of that range or even higher"*, and separately *"we should do better than the lower end of that range."*
- **Q2 carries the FULL minimum-wage impact** — Q1 captured only ~5 weeks (Karnataka effective **23 May**): *"That itself is almost more than double the impact that we had this quarter."*
- **Narrower guidance promised at the Q2 call (October)**, once open-enrolment/AEP bids are finalised — *"most plans would be finalising their bids by this time... we'll get to know specifics only by September."*
- **Full repayment of all outstanding debt during FY27** — *"We remain on track to fully repay our outstanding debt during FY 2027."*
- **Seasonal revenue to remain ~6% of total in FY27**, same proportion as FY26 (it was ~3% / ~$20mn in FY25, rising to ~$50mn / ~6% in FY26 after BroadPath).
- **Minimum-wage mitigation: 12–18 months** to play out fully, via expansion into states outside Karnataka/Telangana plus operational efficiency.
- **AI-led revenue deflation: historically 100–150bps, guided to ~200bps in the near future and "maybe even go higher"** — not tracked quarterly; a broader read promised next quarter.
- **ESOP pool of ~3% of equity** announced but **not yet granted**; spread over multiple years; P&L impact to be reported in a subsequent call.
- **Not guided / declined:** the split of growth between FY26-cohort and legacy clients (*"I don't have those numbers handy... we can come back to you"*), BroadPath's ongoing revenue split, and any quarterly sequential growth rate (*"The 5% may not continue every quarter"*).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Managed-service / outcome-based constructs** — *"we take operational ownership of, and accountability for a large part of the value chain and deliver committed outcomes at a much lower cost."* Still a minority of wins; effort-based FTE/transaction pricing continues alongside.
- **Mid- and small-market expansion** — **55+ mid-market clients** added across BroadPath and CareSeed; cross-sell described as *"pretty high"* opportunity in mid-market, but the CareSeed **platform** is unlikely to sell into large payers (who already have quality-reporting vendors) — only the **combined platform + services package** could.
- **Quality / Medicare Advantage Stars** — new capability, structurally growing as payers chase Stars-linked revenue.
- **M&A pipeline:** three stated target areas — **clinical/care-management capability adjacencies**, the **provider side** (for both capability and client access), and **healthcare technology capabilities**. Explicitly *not* pursuing acquisitions to buy specific clients: *"it's very difficult to do an M&A because somebody is in a specific client... It's mostly around capabilities."*

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- U.S. national health expenditure is projected by CMS to reach 20.3% of GDP by 2033, up from 17.6% in 2023, underscoring market scale and the urgency of improving healthcare administration
- Demographic change - the U.S. Census Bureau identifies 2030 as a turning point when all baby boomers will be over 65 and one in five U.S. residents will be of retirement age, driving more frequent and complex healthcare interactions
- Chronic disease burden (diabetes, cardiovascular, respiratory conditions) drives utilization and reinforces demand for prevention, risk stratification, care coordination and population-level interventions
- Medicare Advantage enrolment continues to increase but growth is maturing and profitability pressure is intensifying, pushing plans to invest in AI, automation, operational efficiency, Stars performance, utilization management, payment integrity and member experience
- Medicaid change from post-pandemic eligibility redeterminations plus funding/eligibility/operational changes under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBB), and expiry of enhanced ACA Marketplace premium subsidies - together increasing membership volatility across Medicaid and Exchange populations and demand for enrollment, eligibility, claims, billing, payment integrity and member engagement capability
- Rising consumer expectations for convenience, transparency, speed and personalization, accelerating demand for responsive, digital, experience-led engagement models
- Shift toward value-based care and migration of care to lower-cost outpatient, ambulatory, virtual and home-based settings, increasing the need for coordination across administrative, clinical and financial workflows
- Clients moving away from fragmented vendor relationships and point solutions toward integrated partners - shifting the basis of competition from scale alone to relevance, integration and end-to-end workflow value
- Competitive intensity rising as technology-native firms, platform providers and diversified services players increase presence, raising the bar on speed, interoperability and measurable outcomes
- AI adoption moving from isolated pilots toward enterprise-scale deployment, favouring providers with domain specificity, regulatory awareness, auditability and human judgment in the loop
- Margin levers cited: operating leverage from scale, execution efficiency, an increasing mix of transformation-led and outcome-based engagements, automation and digital workflows, tight control of discretionary expenses, and the ability to scale back excess capacity after the open enrollment season
- Revenue mix remains rooted in the payer segment with the provider segment seen as an expansion opportunity; BroadPath supports member-facing and seasonal operations during peak enrolment cycles
- Management expects the market to keep shifting toward AI-enabled, platform-supported and more integrated operating models, with clients emphasising partners that reduce administrative waste and deliver measurable outcomes at scale

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- **The minimum-wage shock is bigger than the headline suggests** because of pay-parity cascade: *"not only the folks who are on minimum wages get a hike... There's also cascading impact on people to ensure pay parity across. It impacts a larger portion of people than the base associates."* With **65–70% of headcount in Bangalore and Hyderabad**, that cascade is the whole 120bps.
- **Q1 captured barely a third of it** (Karnataka effective 23 May); **Q2 impact is "more than double"**.
- **The offset is candidly part-FX:** *"Currency has played a part and helped us to retain the guidance... But even otherwise, even in the underlying forecast, we had some efficiency initiatives planned."* The CFO added that hedges *"were taken last year at a much lower value"* — so the FX benefit shows in adjusted EBITDA but the hedge drag lands in **reported EBITDA and EPS**. A real distinction investors should carry.
- **Mitigation levers named:** expand delivery into **states outside Karnataka and Telangana** (<15–20% of headcount today), and step up **operational efficiency** — full mitigation **12–18 months** away.
- **NO pricing power — and management says so plainly:** *"There were no pricing levers that we exercised... Given the situation of our clients, the movement in prices is in the opposite direction. So there's more pricing pressure than any price increases that we would get. So there is no revenue growth because of price increases."* **All growth is volume and scope.**
- **Three structural deflation sources**, cumulatively **100–150bps historically, guided toward 200bps**: (1) **onshore→offshore migration** of client work, (2) automation savings shared back with clients, (3) **AI**.
- **Internal AI is deliberately not a headcount story:** it targets support functions — *"Can I hire more efficiently using AI? Can I train people more efficiently... Today, if I'm taking six weeks to get somebody proficient, can I take the help of AI and reduce the training timeline to four weeks?"* Headcount reduction only happens **when a client authorises AI in their process** (illustratively 100 people → 80).

M&A is capability-led, disciplined on valuation (**RCM targets passed on price**), and structured so that CareSeed's 31.4% EBITDA margin business is **accretive to margin**, not dilutive. A **~3% ESOP pool** is approved-in-process but ungranted — a future, unquantified P&L charge.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Sagility is an asset-light services business, so expansion is expressed as delivery footprint, capability build-out and acquisitions rather than plant capex. The Company delivers services through its tools and platforms and its talent pool from 31 global service delivery locations across India, the Philippines, the U.S., Jamaica and Colombia; the Board's Report notes this multi-geography footprint combines onshore and nearshore locations in the U.S., Jamaica and Colombia with offshore centres in India and the Philippines, a diversified base that reduces dependence on any single country and supports business continuity. Delivery capacity is scaled through people - a workforce of more than 46,000 professionals worldwide, including clinicians and technology specialists - supported by dynamic workforce management, cross-trained talent pools and multi-geo scalable delivery infrastructure that allows capacity to be aligned to fluctuating client volumes. Footprint expansion is also pursued through M&A: the BroadPath Healthcare Solutions acquisition is described as a strategic step towards entering the mid- and small-market segment, broadening the client base and service portfolio, with its integration and contribution extending Sagility's market reach and complementing its service portfolio. Capability expansion is directed at adjacent, higher-value areas - clinical services and pharmacy benefit management, patient support offerings for PBMs and specialty pharmacy players, and scaling end-to-end Revenue Cycle Management within the provider segment - alongside continued investment in AI, platform-led capabilities and integrated operating models that connect fragmented workflows, plus proprietary platform integration inside client workflows to raise switching costs. Cost-side footprint actions include proactive geo-shifts and a multi-shore delivery model to optimise cost structures. Management states that improvements in margins, operational rigor and balance sheet strength have enhanced the Company's capacity to invest with purpose, with investments directed toward initiatives that reinforce competitive advantage. No named plant, site-commissioning or dated capacity-addition project is disclosed in the provided sections.

They gave a **quantified margin bridge in basis points**, split the minimum-wage hit into its in-quarter (₹70mn) and exceptional (₹151mn) components, disclosed the **exact geographic exposure (65–70% of headcount)** that makes the shock large, admitted the FX crutch when asked directly (*"Both, right? Currency has played a part"*), and volunteered the adjusted-vs-reported hedge distinction unprompted. They **refused to raise guidance three times** off a 14.9% CC organic quarter, and refused to extrapolate 5.1% sequential growth (*"I wouldn't read too much into it"*). Two answers were "we'll come back to you" (the FY26-cohort growth split; BroadPath revenue), which for a company that has now made two acquisitions is a fair ask to follow up. The one moment of edge — *"Baidik, you're asking the same question multiple ways"* — read as conviction rather than irritation. Overall this is management being **structurally conservative into a strong quarter**, which is the right posture ahead of a full-quarter wage hit.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
1. **Q2 absorbs the full minimum-wage impact — "more than double" Q1's 40bps** — against a 24–25% guide that is already partly FX-funded.
2. **The margin defence relies on currency.** If the rupee reverses, the 120bps has nothing to lean on but efficiency, which takes **12–18 months**.
3. **Hedges taken at lower rates** mean **reported** EBITDA/EPS will not enjoy the FX benefit that flatters adjusted EBITDA.
4. **No pricing power at all** — stated outright. Growth must come entirely from volume, scope and new logos while clients push prices *down*.
5. **AI deflation is guided to rise from 100–150bps to ~200bps and "maybe even go higher"** — a permanent, self-inflicted revenue headwind inherent to the model.
6. **Client concentration is increasing**, not decreasing — *"if you can see the percentage of our top three, top five, they also continue to increase"* — even as 55+ mid-market clients were bought in.
7. **A top-5 cohort is shrinking** on an onshore→offshore migration. Margin-positive, revenue-negative, and it will recur.
8. **Managed-service deals take 3–6 months of conversation**; the shift to outcome-based revenue is real but slow, and effort-based pricing still dominates.
9. **Only 1 new logo** in Q1's $35.3mn ACV — growth is overwhelmingly farming, not hunting.
10. **Adjusted vs reported gap is wide** (earnouts, SARs, intangible amortisation, the ₹151mn exceptional, the one-time wage item). Every headline metric on this call is an adjusted one.
11. **Open-enrolment volumes unknowable until September** — the single biggest determinant of H2, and management said so.
12. **Peers are reportedly seeing payer spending tighten**; Sagility says it is not, *"at least we are not seeing in the conversations that we are having."* Watch for divergence.
13. **The ~3% ESOP pool** is an unquantified future dilution/charge.
14. **CareSeed's platform may not scale to large payers** — management conceded most large clients already have quality-reporting vendors; only a packaged platform+services play could enter.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- **The Everest data point — 70% of payers have "adopted AI", only 10% see measurable improvement — is the single most valuable disclosure on the call.** It reframes AI from a threat to a BPM's addressable problem: piecemeal AI fails, end-to-end workflow redesign is required, and only a domain-deep operator can do that redesign.
- **Insourcing is economically impossible for cost-pressured payers** because the work sits offshore. Cost pressure on clients is therefore a *tailwind*, not a risk — the exact inverse of the usual outsourcing-cycle worry.
- **Sagility has zero pricing power and is growing 15% CC anyway.** All of it is volume/scope. That is a stronger signal about demand than any pricing-led beat would be.
- **The margin guide is being defended with FX, and management said so.** The underlying operating margin is *not* comfortably absorbing 120bps yet — mitigation is 12–18 months out.
- **Deliberate geographic de-risking has begun** — Indore, Tamil Nadu, Mumbai — driven not by cost arbitrage but by **regulatory wage risk concentration** in Karnataka/Telangana. Expect this to become a structural cost line.
- **CareSeed is tiny ($5.1mn) but bought at 31.4% EBITDA margin with 95% recurring revenue and 26 new logos** — the client list and the Medicare-Advantage quality capability are the assets; the revenue is rounding.
- **Seasonality doubled (3% → 6% of revenue) because of BroadPath**, and is now a permanent feature of the Q1 and Q2 optics. Sequential declines in Q1 are structural, not signals.
- **Attrition improving from 38.1% to 28.6% in one quarter** is a large, under-discussed cost and quality tailwind in a 47,307-person business.
- **Present in only 7 of the top 10 national insurers, and entry to the rest must come through clinical and payment integrity** — the traditional claims/enrolment work at those accounts is already placed elsewhere. That is a precise, checkable roadmap.
